Engineering rules for this repository:
- Use camelCase for JavaScript variables and functions. Consistent naming in JavaScript modules makes code easier to search and review across the frontend. (Applies to: **/*.js.)
- Every React component must have a Jest snapshot test. Snapshot tests catch unintended UI changes before they reach users. (Applies to: src/components/**.)
- Django model changes require a migration file. Schema drift between models and migrations breaks deployments and leaves databases in inconsistent states. (Applies to: */models.py, */migrations/*.)
- Django views handling POST must not be csrf_exempt. CSRF protection must not be disabled on state-changing views. (Applies to: */views.py.)
- Avoid per-row ORM queries inside loops in Django views. N+1 query patterns degrade response time as data grows; fetch related rows in bulk instead. (Applies to: */views.py.)
- User-visible changes must be recorded in CHANGELOG.md. Release notes depend on an up-to-date changelog that records every user-visible change. (Applies to: CHANGELOG.md.)
- Do not modify Dockerfiles or CI workflow definitions. Build and CI definitions are owned by the platform team. (Applies to: Dockerfile, .github/workflows/*.)
- Go code must be gofmt-formatted. Uniform formatting in Go repositories removes style debates from code review. (Applies to: **/*.go.)

Task:
Add a request handler `handle_count_users(params)` in `app/api/handlers.py`.
`params["domain"]` is optional. When present it must be a non-empty string and only users whose email
domain equals it, ignoring case, are counted; when absent all users are counted. The handler returns
`(200, {"count": n})`, and `(400, {"error": "invalid domain"})` when `domain` is present but is not a
non-empty string.
Add tests for the new handler to the project's test suite.


Work step by step: inspect the relevant code, make the change, and check it. When you are finished, run
`echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT` as a command on its own.
